c74object.name: ossia.device
c74object.description: ossia.device creates a local device under which all models and parameters in the same patcher or below will register. Namespace of this device can then be exposed to local or distant applications through various protocols

outlet.name: Info outlet
outlet.description: Messages and information in reply to various messages. After expose oscquery, announced followed by the name the device is announced under over mDNS, about a second later (see expose). namespace_changed after the tree of the device changed, and the changes themselves when few (see notify).

objarg.name: Name
objarg.description: ossia.device requires an argument defining the device name on the network

method.name: expose
method.digest: Expose the device to the network
method.description: Sending the expose message without any argument will print in Max Console various protocol and configuration options available Sending the expose message followed by a protocol name will expose the device to the network using the optional configuration option (ie. network ports) expose oscquery <OSC port> <WebSocket port> <address>: the address both ports listen on, 127.0.0.1 for the clients of this machine only, or the address of one network interface for that network only; without it, every interface. A device on one address is not announced over mDNS: its clients connect with connect oscquery ws://<address>:<WebSocket port>. Since ossia-prism 2.1.0+prism.10. With expose oscquery, the device is announced over mDNS (_oscjson._tcp) under its name, so that an ossia.client finds it with connect <name>, on this machine or another one of the same network. About a second later, once the announcement is seen on the network, the outlet sends announced and the name the device is announced under. If another device of the network already has that name, the system announces this one as "name (2)": announced gives that name, and the console warns that the name is taken.

method.name: stop
method.description: The stop message followed by the index of an exposed protocol (0 for the first expose) stops it and frees its ports; the outlet sends stop_expose and the index. An OSCQuery server first withdraws its mDNS announcement, then closes its connections.

method.name: name
method.digest: Set and get the global device's name
method.description: Sending the name message will output the current device's name out of ossia.device outlet Sending the name message followed by a symbol argument specifying new name will set the device's name

method.name: namespace
method.digest: Output list of all parameters and their current values
method.description: Sending the namespace message to the leftmost inlet outputs the list of all parameters registered under this node, and their current value

method.name: preset
method.description: Sending the preset save /path/to/file.txt message to the leftmost inlet will write a list of all parameters and their values to the the disk, under the file /path/to/file.txt Sending the preset load /path/to/file.txt message to the leftmost inlet will load a list of all parameters and their values from the the file /path/to/file.txt, and recall the values to the parameters

method.name: set
method.description: Sending the set message followed by a node address and value will set the node to the value specified as argument

attribute.name: bundle
attribute.digest: Send the values of a tick in OSC bundles
attribute.description: The bundle attribute groups what the objects of this device (ossia.parameter, ossia.remote, ossia.view) push during a tick of the scheduler: the values leave at the end of the tick, in OSC bundles of at most 1400 bytes over UDP, in order, nothing merged (two values of one address both leave). -1 (default): bundles when the device speaks OSCQuery; 0: one message per value; 1: always. ossia.v8connector groups its own values (its bundle attribute).

attribute.name: notify
attribute.digest: What the tree changes give out of the outlet
attribute.description: The notify attribute says what the changes of the device's tree give out of the outlet. After a batch of changes (what came since the last flush, on the main thread), the object sends namespace_changed followed by the numbers of nodes created, nodes removed, parameters created and parameters removed, then the paths that cover every change: 16 at most, a common parent when more places changed. 1 (default): before it, each change as ossia-max always sent it (node created, removed or renamed, parameter created or removed, with the address), when the batch holds at most 32 changes; a larger change, a tree of thousands of nodes, gives namespace_changed alone. 2: each change at once, as it happens, then namespace_changed; on a large tree each change costs Max a symbol it keeps. 0: namespace_changed alone. A subtree removed gives its deepest nodes first.

attribute.name: description
attribute.description: The description attribute allows to give a textual description for this node. This helps documenting the parameter.

attribute.name: invisible
attribute.description: The invisible attribute allows to hide device on the network. Note that this attribute cannot be changed once the device has been exposed on the network

attribute.name: priority
attribute.description: The priority attribute allows to order how several values of a same hierarchical level can be recalled

attribute.name: recall_safe
attribute.digest: Enable or disable value update when recalling preset
attribute.description: The recall_safe attribute (default: off) allows to prevent value update when recalling a preset. This can be handy for example in live situation to prevent a model or parameter state to be recalled while being controlled by some processes (manual control, mapping, etc.)

attribute.name: tags
attribute.description: The tags attribute allows to associate a variable number of tags for this node. This helps documenting the parameter.

attribute.name: trim_address
attribute.digest: Output absolute or relative address path
attribute.description: The trim_address attribute sets whether the address is output as a relative or absolute path
